Built in one session. Nothing needed asking; everything below is a call the plan left to the builder, or a gap it didn't cover. Run with npm run dev (mock-control at 90c65b9, beside this repo) or node src/build.ts <repo> [commit].

Changed: Libraries and layout

where package.json file page

no quote, so nothing to search for

where src/scip.ts file page

quote const { scip } = require('@sourcegraph/scip-typescript/dist/src/scip.js');

Because (Claude, not asked): the plan left these to the builder. Node 24+ runs the .ts files directly, so there is no build step; tsc only checks. marked parses plans and renders prose. The index is read with the protobuf bindings scip-typescript already ships, a deep import into its dist, pinned to 0.4.0. The spike went through the scip CLI and SQLite instead; that's a second binary to install for one lookup, so I didn't. Modules are one per step: plan, git, scip, resolve, site, render, build, serve. The site's URLs are plans/<cart>/, plans/<cart>/as-built/, files/<path>/, symbols/<file>/<descriptor>/, and profile/, with relative links so the output also opens from file://.

Changed: As-built anchors are shown at the as-built's head, not the plan's base

where src/site.ts file page

quote const commits = d.before && d.before.sha !== sha ? [d.before, generated] : [generated];

Because (Claude, not asked): the plan says each anchor is shown at the plan's base, but pumice's as-built anchors were written after the work. Its assets quote doesn't exist at the base, so showing it there would make the as-built look wrong. Pumice's as-built has a head: field (not in lanyard), so its anchors are shown at that commit and at the generated one. Without a head, only the generated commit is shown. This file has a head for the same reason.

Changed: A SCIP anchor's quote is also looked for inside the symbol's range

where src/resolve.ts file page

quote view.note = `lines ${def.startLine}–${def.endLine}; quote at ${describeLines(marked)}`;

Because (Claude, not asked): pumice's SCIP anchor has a quote, and MockPanel#'s range is lines 9 to 152. Without the quote, a reader can't tell which of 144 lines the entry meant. The quote's lines are highlighted and the view says whether it was found, which is how "matches at da023f1 and not at 90c65b9" shows up on the page. It's still not a drift judgment: both sides are shown and neither is marked wrong.

Changed: A file anchor without a quote is shown, not resolved

where src/site.ts file page

quote ra.note = 'no quote, so nothing to search for';

Because (Claude, not asked): pumice's first as-built entry anchors a README heading path with no quote. The plan's rule is the quote, so there's nothing to search for. Resolving the heading path itself (walking the markdown headings) was the obvious alternative; I declined it because the plan chose quotes, and it's a second resolver for one anchor.

Changed: Which directories get indexed

where src/scip.ts file page

quote return packages.has(JSON.parse(repo.show(sha, f) ?? '{}').name);

Because (Claude, not asked): the plan didn't say, and mock-control's root tsconfig.json has no files of its own. A SCIP symbol names its package, so each directory whose package.json has that name is indexed, using its tsconfig.json, or every tsconfig*.json beside it if there isn't one. Commits are indexed only when an anchor needs them, once each, into a temp checkout from git archive. No cache: about 0.4 seconds a commit didn't earn one.

Changed: Microdata items have no itemtype

where src/render.ts file page

quote items have no <code>itemtype</code>; property names are defined here

Because (Claude, not asked): microdata wants itemtype to be an absolute URL, and the site has no fixed host, nor a domain I should invent. Items are typed by where they sit and by their properties, and the profile defines the names. Worth a decision once there's somewhere real to point.

Changed: Reverse pages list where (new) anchors too

where src/site.ts file page

quote ra.place.refs.push({ plan, doc: d, entry: re, anchor });

Because (Claude, not asked): a new anchor still names a file, and pumice's are mostly in the README. Leaving them off would hide most of what pumice did to that file. They're marked new and not resolved, as the plan says.

Because (Claude, not asked): gimlet's own anchor is mock-control: plans/.... Built against mock-control, that's not another repo. The repo's name is its directory's name, since mock-control has no remote.
